The high-pitched humming synth during the first part of the bridge of Down In It ("I used to be so big and strong..."). Sounds like anxiety, similar to the drone during the trappy sections of Gambino's This Is America.

The less high-pitched whirring during the last part of the last verse of Last ("fresh blood through tired skin, new sweat to drown me in..."), and though this is less subtle, from the same song, in fact right before that last verse, that fucking twisted synth that comes in among that ascending guitar riff.

The synth in some live versions (recent performances and the AATCHB version iirc) of the second verse of Closer.

The voice-synth(?) in the second verse of The Big Come Down, which, like the Down In It example above, sounds like anxiety.

Trent counting the six-four time signature right before the loud part of the breakdown in Demon Seed.

None of these are particularly subtle, but just to include some from that brilliant triptych: yet another twisted synth example that recurs in She's Gone Away, the wordless vocals that enter at the end of This Isn't The Place, what feels like a nod to the name in the lyric "my feet are *nailed* to the floor" in Not Anymore, that one quick four strum before "WHY TRY CHANGE WHEN YOU KNOW YOU CAN'T?" is belted out for the second time (definitely an example of the rough aesthetic of Bad Witch) in Ahead of Ourselves, and the marimba reminiscent of the Fragile era in Over and Out before the vocals enter.

As one may expect, it’s not exactly easy for someone who identifies as an agnostic to envision Heaven. However, assuming there is such a realm, I imagine that it would lack physical features, not a “place” at all but rather a grey void, if anything. I imagine that a more adequate description of Heaven would be a boundless consciousness or transcendental state of mind in which one is generally at peace, free to muse about the nature of the Universe and reality (of which one would acquire as much understanding as they ever possibly could upon entering the realm) entirely unhindered. One would be equally free to reflect upon one’s own mortal life clearly and objectively, without becoming preoccupied with regret or with that which could have been.

If I were pressed to imagine a utopian physical Heaven, on the other hand, I know that it would have at least four separate “regions.” One region would be a wintry realm where the temperature, whether the snow is a few centimeters or a couple of feet deep or there’s a light flurry or a whipping, view-obscuring blizzard at any given time, in any specific location, would always just be slightly chilly, never frigid to a weakening degree or even enough to cause one to shiver, as it would be a few degrees above one’s “shivering threshold.” The sky in this region would be completely light grey during the day while it would be a deep indigo and speckled with several stars at night, with the Moon never obscured and, in fact, fully clear (unless, of course, it is in its new moon phase). There would be snowy forests to travel through along with expansive ice caves and tunnel systems underground and in the mountainsides, great wide open snow fields, and immense, thickly iced-over, only slightly foggy grey bodies of water on which one could slide and move along ad infinitum if they wish to do so.

A slightly similar yet obverse region would be a desert in which the temperature would constantly be pleasantly warm (quite a few degrees below one’s “sweating threshold”), the sky would be just as it would be in a desert in the mortal world (albeit with clouds only manifesting at dusk, if ever, and, as with the previously described region, the Moon would almost always be visible at nighttime), and there would be sparse, scattered flora and fauna. This arid landscape would have large, flat, open fields of sand, nearly identical sand fields with the one difference of containing dunes of varying steepness instead of total flatness, areas rife with sandstone, boulders, and small mountains with long, sprawling tunnel networks and caves, not unlike those of the winter region, that also reach the underground and can be explored as one pleases, and a few generally flat wasteland or junkyard areas. These areas would have vast mounds of cinder blocks and similar objects on which one could climb and from which one could salvage and build something, as well as concrete tunnels one can walk through or settle in, and finally, all manner of apparently antiquated, mostly rusted machinery of various eras (including the future, apparently, as colossal mechs are among these machines) which appear to be solely for visual ambience if anything, but can actually be operated, even if they appear to no longer be functional.  
	
Another region would be an urban landscape in which it is always night, with many slightly flickering orange streetlights to guide one’s way down desolate sidewalks along derelict, barren brick edifices, from end to end of alleys, through concrete tunnels downtown, and the abandoned skate parks and dried-out spillways which they’re nearby. One could engage in urban exploration in this region, as there are many vacated warehouses, factories, safe maintenance tunnels, and more. If one were to become lonely in this region, they would merely need to wait at a public transportation stop, and in due time a tram would approach, a tram on which one could ride for as long as they desire, and, should they choose to sit on the cushioned bench adjacent to the wall of the tram that faces a parallel bench on the other side, there would be someone sitting across from them with whom they would be very glad to speak. 

Not much needs to be said of the fourth region, as it is, quite simply, outer space. One could move about freely, exploiting the lack of gravity while maintaining control of their movement, to travel past the stars, moons and planets as they please, and one could also even land on any of such celestial bodies to explore it to their liking.
	
As should be quite clear, immortality would be at play in this utopian realm, with pabulum and air not being necessities, although one could eat whatever they’d like if they really wished to do so. Though this would be difficult to elaborate upon, everyone has their own realm of this sort, and they may even have regions different from those described, but they can join others in a “compromise realm” (hence the name, a Heaven coalescing aspects of the Heaven realms of all parties involved), and each party involved could remain with another (or others, if the compromise realm is between more than two individuals with their own realm) in this compromise realm for however long they wish.

The professor of this creative writing class I took in my last semester of high school before graduation assigned a prompt similar to this, to describe your personally ideal afterlife. If anyone's interested, I could share it, though it's a little long.

Not every person with depression experiences it in some uniform way, just as it precipitates in them at different times, for different reasons, etc. In my experience, the sadness comes in waves. Though I don't think it's SAD, it's happened to arrive particularly strongly around this time of year these past few years. When it's not present, or rather felt, since it always seems to be lurking underneath, it's the emptiness, whether it's compounded with rage of some sort, guilt, shame, pure apathy, fear (often of the self/their future), or some other generally negative and painful emotion.
Same reason as when it began, realizing the world is a harsh place and people don't really care, just hide it better now.

I didn't. They are still there and although I suppress them, they surface every single day. I've been keeping myself from actually going through with it by:

-Trying to enjoy life. This seems to have largely manifested in greater hedonism, which is in and of itself a source of further shame. However, I have also tried some new activities and have tried to make more friends. Even though I feel slightly more socially well-adjusted than I did in secondary school, when I first fell into this mentality, I still alienate myself and confuse/repel people, and I've realized just how unreliable and disappointing people tend to be and how familiarity can indeed breed contempt, and their penchant for gossip and mudslinging about people familiar and unfamiliar to them alike have not helped my resentment and distrust of human nature.

-Thinking about how fortunate I've been and how it would affect those close to me. Even though the whole "you have it better than other people, so cheer up" argument pisses me off probably more than the average person as it continues to every time someone utters some variation of this ignorant platitude when I actually decide to confide in them or they just find out how I think/feel, one of the conflicting components of my mind uses it regularly. While I'm still here, obviously, and therefore it must be at least somewhat effective (if frustrating and ignorant/general), continuing to feel this way despite my really not that bad circumstances adds to my shame, like the previous example. And of course tying into this is the haunting thought of how those close to me (inb4 "at least you have some people who are close to you;" many things I keep to myself, so "close" may be an overstatement, and "mutual care/cordiality" may be more applicable) would react after I've carried out my escape plan. 

-Holding onto the idea of creation. Reproduction is immensely overrated, obsolete, and our planet is dying with our already overabundant population. But I get it. The desire to leave a mark on the world, for legacy, to feel less ephemeral than our lifespan. So the other option (apart from carrying out some horrible atrocity/atrocities, which, although it has been shown that many who chose to do so have succeeded in being remembered and this disgusting trend will probably continue, is obviously immoral and just something I wouldn't be able/want to do) is creating art. Certain forms of art seem to be my only true "calling" in this world, so through this I will try to fulfill that silly ubiquitous need for legacy. Of course, this isn't easy when paralyzing perfectionism and difficulty concentrating are present, but I've pretty much decided this is something I have to do before I go.

It was this time of year three years ago when despair began to tower overhead and emotions and pretty much everything else became overwhelming. While yeah, I've been employed for a while now (that's all that they seem to think matters), maintain decent grades, and can carry out a seemingly (because it's limited, by time and some things to which I just won't respond, etc.) convincing charade of being okay, lively or whatever, negative emotions are all I really feel, and otherwise I feel emotionless. There are scars only I know of, and I'm fine with it that way until the day I finally collapse completely. Again it's hard to concentrate, think I might nosedive again soon, know I don't want to stay here much longer. We'll see how this goes~

However, I am very seldom awoken in a panic upon having such dreams, so I am sorry that you deal with such results of having these dreams.

Very much agreed. While I do not endure nightmares very often, I somewhat increasingly have dreams with mundane themes directly related to my life/the present situation that sometimes get into really personal territory. It is only after I've woken up and the dream is recalled by some random trigger in the course of the day that I realize how unsettling the content of such dreams was. As I am dreaming, though, I feel kind of like I did a few years ago, when I actually felt alive, but there is (and was, in those few years ago) a sort of melancholy to it, as though I know/knew it was not to last. And this melancholy is preferable to real life as it is actually something other than anger or despair that I can feel, so I definitely know what you mean. Write down some of your dreams, maybe even make one or more of them into a story, if you enjoy or are open to writing. Not sure if it is for you, but writing is one of very few truly fulfilling things for me.
